clue.text: Chose top set to make an instrument

indicators.note: the words are used to make something new, so their letters are rearranged into the instrument

explanation.surface: Picking out the best set of players to form a band or orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' signals that the eleven letters of CHOSE TOP SET are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's listening device is a medical instrument.

clue.text: Scenery for television performance?

parts.note: a television is a TV set
a piece is a work performed, such as a musical piece

explanation.surface: Asking whether a broadcast show counts as theatrical backdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre a free-standing piece of stage scenery is called by this name.

clue.text: Present eastern eleven or ten in a way

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and also a sports team

indicators.note: the number is placed inside the road abbreviation

parts.note: ST, street, is a way or road

explanation.surface: Introducing a team from the East, or perhaps ten players, in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift or the here and now, but is the adjective 'in being'. 'or' is only a link; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something present is currently in being, which is to exist.

clue.text: Increase right for a rambler

parts.note: a hike is a rise, as in a price hike

explanation.surface: Asking for a pay rise on behalf of a country walker.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is one who walks for pleasure in the countryside.

clue.text: Important part of defence

explanation.surface: A key element of a team's or army's defensive line.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means most noticeable or significant; in military use it is a bulge in a defensive line projecting towards the enemy.

clue.text: It could be no let up for the wealthy

indicators.note: the phrase suggests these words could become something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The rich face relentless pressure, with no respite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It could be' tells you to rearrange the letters of NO LET UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent describes great riches and lavish luxury.

clue.text: I came up, dined and died, being very lean

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to have dined is to have eaten, ATE
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone arrives, eats and then expires, looking very thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns I CAME round to give EMACI; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin, typically from starvation or illness.

clue.text: Half assume the total

indicators.note: half of the word's six letters are taken, a run of three from within it

explanation.surface: Guessing at the total figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes three of the six letters of ASSUME, here the run from its third to fifth letters rather than either end.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is the result of adding numbers together.

clue.text: Poles accept nothing for a slipshod worker

indicators.note: the poles take in the zero, so that word sits between them

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
love is nothing, a score of zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Polish workers agreeing to take no pay, branded careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is the abbreviations S and N for the two geographical poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloven is someone habitually untidy or careless in their work.

clue.text: Insect that might be airborne

parts.note: may expresses possibility, what might happen
to fly is to be in the air

explanation.surface: A creature that may possibly take to the air.
explanation.definitionFit: This short-lived winged creature is an insect of rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Credit about right to deceive

indicators.note: the credit word goes around the letter for right

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Lending money on the right terms in order to swindle someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To trick someone is to fool or dupe them.

clue.text: Celebrate with a Conservative expressing praise

parts.note: to laud is to praise or celebrate
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Throwing a party with a Tory politician, full of compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudatory means full of commendation.

clue.text: Barge in and engrave Iron with soldiers

parts.note: read as en-grave, putting into a grave, which is to bury or inter
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Interrupting a craftsman cutting letters into metal while troops look on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engrave' looks like carving; it is read as en-grave, to put in a grave. RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle or intrude in others' affairs is to barge in.

clue.text: Excellent notion left behind

indicators.note: the letter for left comes after the notion, behind it

parts.note: an idea is a notion

explanation.surface: A fine thought someone forgot and left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect, as good as can be, is excellent.

clue.text: Setting in which to study biblical extract

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a text is a passage of scripture used for a sermon

explanation.surface: Background against which to read a passage from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The surroundings or circumstances in which something happens are its setting.

clue.text: Direction to draw up underground

parts.note: a fox's underground den is an earth

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: An instruction to dig and pull something up from below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DRAW to WARD. An earth is a fox's burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Towards the ground is a direction of travel.

clue.text: Thank-you-note from gallery

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A letter of thanks sent by an art museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ta' is British slang for thanks; the Tate is a famous group of London art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate is a well-known art museum in London.

clue.text: One in Paris must turn up in a moment for a tablet

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes inside the word for an instant

parts.note: taken as the word itself, an instant

indicators.note: in a down clue, turn up means the letters are read backwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: un is French for one

explanation.surface: A Frenchman must suddenly appear in a hurry for a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses the French word, read upwards in a down clue; 'in' puts it inside the instant. 'must' and 'for a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorial tablet set up to commemorate someone is a monument.

clue.text: Companion in at ten with the German

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A friend who turns up at ten o'clock with a German man.
explanation.definitionFit: One who accompanies or is present alongside another is a companion.

clue.text: Former monarch I had to follow in network

indicators.note: the contraction comes after the king's initials, following them

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George, a former monarch
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A deposed king's confession of being caught up in a web.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a lattice or network of lines.

clue.text: Cashier one Sergeant Major in Norfolk town

indicators.note: the soldier and the numeral go inside the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, England
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A senior soldier working as a cashier in a small East Anglian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' looks like a bank worker but is the verb: to cashier is to dismiss from the armed forces. Diss is a town in Norfolk, a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to discharge them in disgrace.

clue.text: Gradually disappear as a film may do

explanation.surface: Slowly vanishing, like the end of a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle gently away is to fade; a film's closing shot dims to black in the same way.

clue.text: Voluntarily avoid an ancestor IS 1

explanation.surface: Choosing to steer clear of a forefather.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from something is to hold back from it; a forebear, also spelt this way, is a forefather.

clue.text: A soft fruit or so it would seem

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A squashy piece of fruit, or so it looks.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the impression of being something is to seem.

clue.text: Type of cleaner with nothing in it

explanation.surface: A household appliance that turns out to be empty.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoover-style appliance is a vacuum cleaner, and a vacuum is a space empty of all matter.

clue.text: Girl who is soft with everyone

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
each means every one

explanation.surface: A girl who is a pushover with everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peach' is old-fashioned slang for an attractive girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A lovely young woman was once called a real stunner or a peach.

clue.text: Sacred writing consisting of text by river

indicators.note: the river is placed beside the text, next to it

parts.note: a script is a written text
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Holy words made up of writing produced beside a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire; 'consisting of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy writ, such as the Bible, is sacred writing.

clue.text: Absolutely vertical and true at Lords

explanation.surface: Perfectly upright and honest, as at the home of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; a pitch described this way is flat and true, good for batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumb can mean utterly (plumb crazy), exactly perpendicular, and of a cricket pitch, even and reliable.

clue.text: Bird taking vital turn to the east is inclined to rivalry

parts.note: an emu is a large flightless bird

indicators.note: the word vital takes a turn, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird making a crucial change of direction eastward, keen to compete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is the anagram signal for 'vital', whose rearranged letters sit between the bird and the compass point; 'taking' and 'to the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Being emulative means striving to equal or outdo others, which is competitiveness.

clue.text: Set vertically and end up in reverse

indicators.note: the two words are taken in the opposite order to the one printed

explanation.surface: Stand something on its head and finish backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' swaps the order of the words END UP, not their letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something on its end, upright, is to set it vertically.

clue.text: Deliberately collide with an animal

explanation.surface: Purposely crashing into a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram is to strike with force on purpose; a ram is a male sheep.

clue.text: Broadcaster responsible for sparks

explanation.surface: A radio presenter who causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster spreads things widely, as does one who hands out goods; in an engine the distributor routes current to each spark plug.
